clue.text: Look back inside light and push, connecting electrical device

indicators.note: looking back means the word for look is read from its end to its start
one piece sits inside another, so the word for light is opened up to take it

blocks.note: to peer is to look closely
thin, as in light or slight
to plug a product is to push or promote it

explanation.surface: Instructions for wiring something up: glance back at the lamp, then press to connect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' tempts as a lamp, but it means slender. The reversed look is wrapped after the first two letters of that word, not round the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard British mains connector has three pins, so the three-pin plug is a familiar electrical fitting.

clue.text: Expression of discontent arrives in sulk before start of holidays

indicators.note: one piece placed in another means the sulk word wraps round the arrivals abbreviation
the start of a word is its first letter only

blocks.note: to have the hump is to be in a sulk
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives
first letter of holidays

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling and sulking just before the holidays begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Having the hump is British slang for sulking; ARR goes after its H, and the H from holidays ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrumph is the throat-clearing noise a person makes to show disapproval or irritation.

clue.text: Tuscan island fit for uprising?

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the word from the bottom upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: fit, as in capable

explanation.surface: Is this island off Tuscany a suitable place to stage a revolt?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Napoleon, exiled to this island, who escaped it to rise again.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba lies off the Tuscan coast of Italy and is famous as Napoleon's place of exile.

clue.text: Plague in spleen etc, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect hints the letters are not to be trusted as given and need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor guessing that a plague has reached the spleen and other organs.
explanation.walkthrough: The I belongs to the fodder as well as the indicator phrase: only 'suspect' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, the same thing as a plague.

clue.text: Naval commander embraced by colonels only

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so the answer sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An admiral welcomed exclusively by army colonels.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral who won at Trafalgar, the archetypal naval commander.

clue.text: Produce milk for baby: feat feeding past midnight?

indicators.note: feeding into something puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: a feat is an act or deed
after midnight it is late

explanation.surface: A tired mother managing the night feed long after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeding' looks like part of the baby picture but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lactate is to secrete milk from the breasts, as a nursing mother does.

clue.text: Unspecific award for old US leader

blocks.note: general, as opposed to specific
a grant is a sum awarded

explanation.surface: A vague prize handed to a former American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant led the Union army as general and later became US president.

clue.text: Hammer: force nailing everything

indicators.note: nailing pins something in place, here read as holding a piece inside

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force
all means everything

explanation.surface: Using a hammer, apply force to nail everything down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the everyday name for London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet is a hammer with a large wooden or rubber head.

clue.text: Sunny market

blocks.note: first meaning: fine weather, clear and bright
second meaning: a gathering for selling goods or livestock

explanation.surface: A bright day for the market stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is bright and dry, and a fair is a periodic market or trade gathering.

clue.text: Coming from church, what might Rosemary say confidently to Herb?

blocks.note: surface padding: framing the reply as spoken by a woman named Rosemary
basil is a herb, and also a man's name
a confident reply: I can

explanation.surface: A woman named Rosemary reassuring a man named Herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary, Basil and Herb are all herbs and names; Rosemary addresses him as Basil, telling him 'I can'.
explanation.definitionFit: Basilican is the adjective for a basilica, a type of large church, so it describes things belonging to one.

clue.text: Book that's brilliant about popular music

blocks.note: bright means brilliant
on, as in concerning
rock is a style of popular music

explanation.surface: A review of a great book on pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton rock is also a seaside stick of sweet candy, but here it is the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is Graham Greene's 1938 novel about a teenage gangster.

clue.text: Come and see bread after it's risen?

blocks.note: first meaning: a showman's cry inviting the crowd to gather
second meaning: a small loaf, with up for having risen

explanation.surface: A baker inviting people to admire a loaf that has risen.
explanation.definitionFit: Roll up! is the fairground barker's invitation; a bread roll that has risen is, playfully, a roll up.

clue.text: Rubbish is around square

indicators.note: rubbish, used as a verb, means to trash or wreck, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Litter lying around a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a place where the rubbish lies; it is the definition, an old-fashioned person.
explanation.definitionFit: A square is a conventional, out-of-touch person, and so is a dinosaur in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Spirit about to be put in mixture of ale and punch

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters of the drinks are stirred into a new order
one piece is put in another, so it is placed inside the mixed letters

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink spirit about to be added to a bowl of ale and punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests alcohol among the ale and punch, but it means a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A leprechaun is a mischievous sprite of Irish folklore, a kind of spirit or fairy.

clue.text: Crack — mentally and physically?

blocks.note: surface reading: to break down under emotional strain
setter's reading: the same phrase also means literally to break into fragments

explanation.surface: Someone cracking up both in mind and in body.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose emotional control, while literally it describes something shattering into bits.

clue.text: Odd bits of toenails, dark greenish-blue

indicators.note: the odd bits are the letters in odd-numbered positions: first, third, fifth, seventh

blocks.note: letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of toenails

explanation.surface: Bits of toenail that have turned a nasty dark blue-green colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Teal is the colour named after the duck's head markings, a deep blue-green shade.

clue.text: Sink filled with fifty fish

indicators.note: a vessel filled with something holds it inside

blocks.note: a ship that founders sinks
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A kitchen sink holding fifty fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' reads as a kitchen basin, but it is the verb founder.
explanation.definitionFit: The flounder is a flatfish, found in coastal waters and estuaries.

clue.text: Unopened post bag

indicators.note: something unopened has lost its opening, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: a stake is a wooden post

explanation.surface: A sealed mailbag that nobody has opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' and 'bag' suggest a mailbag; post is a stake and bag is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is to capture or seize it, which is to take it.

clue.text: Cheap clothes reserved, minimum of cash invested

indicators.note: invested means put into, so one piece goes inside another
the smallest part of a word is taken to be its first letter

blocks.note: kit is clothing or gear
a reserved person is shy
first letter of cash

explanation.surface: Budget clothing set aside after paying very little money for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitschy things are gaudy and in poor taste, which is cheap in the sense of tacky.

clue.text: Home builder: reliable chap joining broody female?

blocks.note: a brick is a dependable person
a layer is a laying hen

explanation.surface: A dependable man pairing up with a woman longing for children while building a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone a brick is old-fashioned British praise for a steadfast friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer builds walls of houses from bricks, so is literally a builder of homes.

clue.text: Colour lacking in bottle

blocks.note: first meaning: the hue of lemons and buttercups
second meaning: short of nerve, cowardly

explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, so lacking in bottle means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is both a primary colour and a long-standing slang word for cowardice.

clue.text: Yours truly is unfortunately up for meat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: yours truly means the speaker, so 'I am', shortened
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A writer confessing they are sadly ready for a meal of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, seasoned sausage meat served in slices.

clue.text: Bird enthusiast with warm eggs

blocks.note: a nut is a fanatic, as in health nut
to hatch eggs is to brood them warm

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher keeping eggs warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird that climbs tree trunks headfirst.

clue.text: Knight at home touring large European capital

indicators.note: touring goes all round something, so the outer pieces wrap around another

blocks.note: to dub is to knight with a sword's touch
at home means in
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A knight who stays home while also touring a large European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital city of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Wading bird in flock, no tail

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the following letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A wading bird among the flock that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No tail' looks like a deletion instruction; it simply supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a stocky sandpiper-like wader that gathers in huge flocks on mudflats.

clue.text: Ocean waves increase a further time

indicators.note: waves move water about, so the letters are churned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a gain is an increase

explanation.surface: The sea's waves are getting bigger yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ocean waves' reads as a phrase; waves is a verb working on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Once again means one more time, a repetition, so it matches a further time.

clue.text: Fate when state of mind reversed

indicators.note: reversed tells the solver to read the word from its end to its start

blocks.note: a mood is a state of mind

explanation.surface: Destiny that turns when one's outlook changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is one's fate, especially a grim or ruinous destiny.

clue.text: Initials on item used for entering a couple of flats, possibly?

blocks.note: a key lets you enter a door
initials can serve as a signature

explanation.surface: Personal initials engraved on the key to a pair of apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B puts B first. Flats look like apartments but are musical flat signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A key signature is the set of sharps or flats at the start of a stave; two flats indicate B-flat major.
